liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Playing In The Band** (3 reviews): The second-set circle jam is great; the Playin'/UJB/Morning Dew/UJB/Playin' sequence is called a must-have; Playin' runs over ten minutes and is very jazzy and improvisational, reminiscent of Mind Left Body Jam [4][11][12]
- **Bertha** (1 review): Bertha starts slowly, but the solo gets the energy moving [13]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Jack Straw has strong speed-ups and slow-downs, with excellent Jerry [13]
- **Tennessee Jed** (1 review): The Tennessee Jed jam turns nicely weird and befuddled [13]
- **Uncle John's Band** (1 review): The move into Uncle John's Band is described as magical [11]
- **Morning Dew** (1 other source): A 22-second patch in Morning Dew comes from the shnid 3290 source, pitch-corrected to match [2]

## Setlist highlights

- **Uncle John's Band Reprise**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 13 archived performances [15]
- Earliest performances in the archive: Playing Reprise [15]

## The recordings

- **gd73-11-10.sbd.unknown.3290.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 23 songs; 152 min; rated 3.72/5 by 18 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer suspects a speed problem in this version, hoping it gets fixed; Reviewer hears no pitch problem in this source and suggests Jerry's playing just sounds fast and fierce; Reviewer agrees the tape sounds sped up, at times approaching a chipmunk sound [4][5][6][7][8][10][11]
- **gd1973-11-10.140704.set1p.set2p.sbd.pcm.miller.clugston.flac1644**: soundboard; 8 songs; 70 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended; remembers the band sounding wired and jangly, and it was their first solo Dead show [7]
- Attendee says the band was on edge all night and the show was intense [9]
- Attendee recalls a party atmosphere at Winterland and a weekend of nonstop good vibes [10]
- Unlike most Winterland shows, it never hit all-out party mode; that came the next night [9]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd73-11-10.sbd.unknown.3290.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Suggests the source may be a cassette generation, given the pitch behavior; Source is a master soundboard reel transferred to PCM, then DAT, then CD [1][8]
- **gd1973-11-10.140704.set1p.set2p.sbd.pcm.miller.clugston.flac1644**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Partial Show Source Info: Master Soundboard Reel > PCM; Transfer Info: PCM (Sony SL-10) > Sony PCM-601ESD > Behringer Ultramatch Pro > Tascam DA-3000 > Adobe… [2]
